jobs.description:
Location: Los Angeles, CA or San Diego, CA or San Francisco, CA or Sacramento, CA

Salary: $235,000 - $245,000 Annually

Organization Overview

Founded in 2004, Brilliant Corners provides innovative housing and housing-related services to those transitioning from or at risk of homelessness or institutionalization. We develop, own, and manage multi-family supportive housing and licensed residential care homes. Additionally, we implement a broad array of scattered-site, one-on-one supportive housing, and clinical case management programs through partnerships with developmental services, homeless services, veteran services, and health care sectors.

In short, we do good work.

We have offices statewide with a staff of passionate people. While we are growing rapidly, we are also selective: We're seeking inspired, talented people who want to be effecting profound change and who have fun doing it.

Department Summary

Brilliant Corners' Housing Services Department is nationally recognized for its role in designing and operating supportive housing solutions that help individuals exit homelessness and avoid institutionalization. We serve individuals with complex needs, including those involved in healthcare, behavioral health, and criminal justice systems.

Our work spans major regions across California, with teams operating in Los Angeles, San Diego, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Sacramento Counties. Across this statewide footprint, the Department operates a diverse and growing portfolio of housing and supportive services programs designed to help individuals access and maintain stable housing.

Position Summary

The Chief Program Officer (CPO) is responsible for the overall vision, strategy, performance, and sustainability of a large and complex portfolio of supportive housing and related programs across California. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and serving as a member of Brilliant Corners' Executive Team, the CPO will provide executive leadership for the Department while ensuring strong alignment with broader organizational priorities. The CPO will oversee the Department's Deputy Chief Program Officers and other senior leaders, creating the conditions for them and the teams they lead to succeed.

This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution. The CPO will ensure strong day-to-day program performance while setting the longer-term direction of the Department, strengthening statewide systems and practices, and ensuring that growth is supported by the infrastructure, leadership capacity, and financial resources necessary to sustain it. A central responsibility will be bringing together the operational and program development functions of Housing Services ensuring alignment across regional program operations, program design and policy, quality assurance, evaluation, and client participation to build consistency statewide while preserving regional flexibility.

The CPO will provide executive oversight across Brilliant Corners' core program areas:

Flexible Housing Pool (Flex Pool): A systems-level model that aligns and deploys housing resources across healthcare, homelessness, and behavioral health systems to rapidly connect individuals to permanent housing. Acting as a centralized intermediary, the Flex Pool braids funding streams, engages landlords, and leverages the private rental market to reduce time to housing and improve long-term stability
Intensive Case Management Services (ICMS): Person-centered, housing-focused services delivered across a range of settings and populations, always grounded in a Housing First approach to help individuals with complex needs successfully obtain and retain housing
Managed Care and Behavioral Health Partnerships: Strategic collaborations with Managed Care Plans, County Behavioral Health Departments, and public systems to deliver housing-based interventions that improve health outcomes. This includes implementing CalAIM Housing Supports, administering Transitional Rent, and supporting housing pathways tied to the Behavioral Health Services Act (BHSA) and other emerging initiatives across complex funding streams and regulatory environments
Program Quality, Evaluation, and Client Participation: Statewide infrastructure and cross-functional teams dedicated to quality assurance, program evaluation, policy development, and meaningful client participation, ensuring programs remain effective, equitable, consistent, and responsive

Additionally, the CPO will serve as one of Brilliant Corners' most senior external representatives to government agencies, Managed Care Plans, healthcare and behavioral health systems, philanthropic partners, and other stakeholders. They will help shape and advance sustainable funding and contracting models that allow Brilliant Corners and its partners to deliver effective, person-centered services at scale. This is a unique opportunity for a seasoned leader to guide one of Brilliant Corners' largest bodies of work at a moment of significant growth and change, while advancing Housing First, housing justice, and high-quality services for thousands of Californians.

Position Responsibilities

Statewide Program Strategy and Performance

Set the strategic direction for Brilliant Corners' Housing Services Department and ensure strong execution across its statewide portfolio. Establish clear priorities, performance expectations, and accountability structures across Flex Pool, case management, managed care, behavioral health, and other housing programs. Balance statewide consistency with the unique needs of individual regions, programs, funders, and communities.

Executive Leadership and Leadership Development

Lead, coach, and support the Department's Deputy Chief Program Officers and other senior leaders, cultivating a high-performing and collaborative leadership team. Create clear roles, strong accountability, and effective structures for decision-making and communication. Invest in leadership development and succession planning throughout the Department while fostering a culture in which staff can grow, thrive, and do their best work.

Program Quality, Evaluation, and Client Participation

Provide executive oversight of statewide quality assurance, program evaluation, policy development, and client participation efforts. Ensure that these functions are meaningfully integrated into program operations and used to improve service quality, client experience, equitable outcomes, and organizational learning. Champion the use of data, client voice, staff expertise, and evidence-informed practice to drive continuous improvement.

Program Development, Innovation, and Growth

Guide the design, development, and implementation of new programs and partnerships, ensuring that growth is aligned with Brilliant Corners' mission, strategic priorities, organizational capacity, and financial sustainability. Support the Department in adapting to emerging opportunities across homelessness, healthcare, behavioral health, and other public systems while maintaining the integrity of the Brilliant Corners model.

Financial Sustainability and Contract Stewardship

Partner closely with Finance and other organizational leaders to oversee the financial health of the Housing Services portfolio. Ensure programs are supported by sustainable budgets, appropriate staffing models, sound contract structures, and effective management of complex and braided funding streams. Identify financial and operational risks early and work collaboratively to develop solutions that protect both service quality and organizational sustainability.

External Partnerships and Systems Leadership

Build and maintain trusted relationships with government agencies, Managed Care Plans, healthcare and behavioral health systems, philanthropy, community partners, and other stakeholders. Represent Brilliant Corners in senior-level conversations related to supportive housing policy, program design, funding, and implementation. Advocate for contracting and funding approaches that support sustainable organizations, a strong workforce, and effective services for the people and communities we serve.

Organizational Alignment and Cross-Functional Partnership

Serve as an active member of Brilliant Corners' Executive Team and ensure strong coordination between Housing Services and organizational partners including Finance, People Operations, Data & Technology, Business Operations, Strategic Partnerships, and other departments. Translate organizational priorities into effective departmental strategies while bringing the experience and needs of Housing Services into enterprise-wide planning and decision-making.

Housing First, Equity, and Person-Centered Practice

Champion Housing First and ensure that person-centered, equitable approaches remain foundational to program design and service delivery. Work with staff, funders, and partners to identify and reduce barriers to housing and services. Advance Brilliant Corners' commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging through both how the Department serves clients and how it supports and develops its workforce.

Requirements

Professional Experience

At least 12 years of progressively responsible experience in human services, supportive housing, homelessness, healthcare, behavioral health, nonprofit leadership, public systems, or a related field
Demonstrated executive leadership experience with increasing levels of organizational responsibility, including success leading large, complex teams and managing senior leaders or leaders of leaders
Experience overseeing complex, multi-program and/or multi-region portfolios with significant operational and financial responsibility
Experience designing, implementing, or overseeing Housing First, supportive housing, case management, or related programs strongly preferred
Experience working with government agencies, healthcare systems, Managed Care Plans, philanthropy, or other institutional funders strongly preferred

Strong financial acumen, including experience overseeing large budgets, government contracts, complex funding streams, and financially sustainable program models
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain senior-level relationships with public agencies, funders, healthcare partners, community organizations, and other external stakeholders

jobs.title: Chief Program Officer - Mental Health, Housing & Homeless Programs
jobs.description:
The Chief Program Officer (CPO) is a senior executive and key member of BACS's Executive Team, serving as the CEO's primary service operating partner. The CPO holds full P&L responsibility and signing authority across all program operations — a $150M+ organization spanning 700+ staff, 100+ funding streams, and 100+ program, residential, and housing sites currently spanning Sacramento to San Mateo Counties. This includes the administrative and service/clinical direction of direct-service programs serving individuals with serious mental illness, substance use disorders, chronic health conditions, and housing instability or homelessness, across the full scope of care at BACS. The CPO is the operational head and primary interfacing executive with funders, county and state partners, and community stakeholders agency-wide, and ensures excellence across clinical, administrative, fiscal, compliance, human resources, and quality improvement functions. This role requires a dynamic, hands-on leader who moves fluidly between C-suite strategy and on-the-ground presence at program sites, operating with a high degree of independence and executive judgment, and who can be trusted to run agency operations at the highest standard without close oversight.

Duties And Responsibilities

Serves as the CEO's primary executive partner in leading agency-wide program operations, stepping in as a trusted #2 across strategic and operational decision-making alongside other C-suite leaders
Owns full P&L accountability for the entire program operations portfolio, including revenue, expenses, and margin performance across all funding streams; proactively identifies and acts on financial risk or underperformance
Directs that services are delivered in full compliance with all applicable funding streams (100+) and regulatory requirements across county, state, and federal contracts
Provides executive oversight, coaching, and accountability for VPs, Directors, and site leadership across the full geographic service area; monitors their performance and financial results, and reviews these with the CEO on a regular basis
Partners with Finance and HR to ensure programs are fiscally sound, appropriately staffed, and operationally compliant — with fluency in budget, HR, and compliance data sufficient to identify and resolve issues independently
Designs and enforces a consistent, high-quality service delivery model across all sites, grounded in BACS's mission, vision, and values, and centered on consumer-driven, strength-based, culturally relevant care
Leads agency-wide Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) systems and standards
Owns contract compliance, grant management, funder reporting, and funder relationships across all funding streams; reviews, negotiates, and preps major contracts for approval
Proactively identifies risk before it materializes; owns the agency-wide Risk Management Plan and associated metrics
Builds and maintains strong, trust-based relationships with funders, government partners, and community organizations
Maintains regular, visible presence across all program, residential, and housing sites agency-wide (Sacramento to San Mateo County); travels routinely as a core function of the role, and proactively communicates across internal departments without relying on others to do so
Identifies operational risk and inefficiency proactively, and acts decisively — without requiring day-to-day direction
Participates in new program development, including grant writing, funder presentations, and external representation of BACS
Leads and models a culture of accountability, excellence, and continual learning across the organization
Other duties as assigned

COMPETENCIES

Operates independently at a true C-suite level; does not require day-to-day management or micromanagement
Strong influencing and negotiating skills; excellent oral and written communication; demonstrated history of building and leveraging high-level relationships with funders, government partners, boards, and staff at all levels; politically savvy
Demonstrated P&L management experience at a large-scale, multi-program, multi-site level
Demonstrated financial, HR, compliance, and QI acumen sufficient to direct and improve agency-wide systems
High integrity and accountability; holds self and others to a standard of excellence
Resilient, adaptable, and effective in a fast-paced, high-complexity environment
Strategic thinker and visionary, balanced with a hands-on, roll-up-your-sleeves operating style
Strength-based, person-centered orientation across housing and behavioral health operations; embraces diversity in all aspects of leadership

Qualifications

Master's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related field required, along with at least ten years of progressive senior leadership experience in behavioral health, homelessness, and/or housing services, including experience operating at a COO/CPO or equivalent executive level
Demonstrated success leading large-scale, multi-site, multi-funder nonprofit or governmental operations (ideally $100M+ budget), with full P&L ownership
Demonstrated direct experience working with the full range of subpopulations served by BACS, including individuals with serious mental illness (SMI), substance use disorders (SUD), chronic and co-occurring health conditions, and housing-insecure/unhoused individuals
Strong working knowledge of behavioral health, housing, and homelessness funding and regulatory frameworks (e.g., MHSA, HUD, Medi-Cal, county contracts)
Demonstrated capacity leading diverse, multi-disciplinary teams across dispersed geographic sites
LCSW, MFT, or equivalent clinical licensure strongly preferred. Lived experience preferred
Proficiency in Microsoft Word/Excel and standard business systems

Physical Requirements

This position requires regular travel throughout the service area and frequent presence at program, residential, and housing sites, in addition to site-based work. Requires the ability to sit, stand, walk, and drive for extended periods; occasional lifting of up to 20 lbs.; dexterity for computer use and documentation; and the ability to see, hear, and speak effectively across in-person and virtual settings. This position is not remote.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Competitive salary of $300,00 -350,000 per year, exempt
100% employer-paid medical, dental, and life insurance coverage options for employees, plus a vision reimbursement program. Children’s healthcare coverage is available for as little as $25/month. Average employer-paid benefit value: approximately $913/month per enrolled individual. BACS contributions apply to company-sponsored plans only.
31 days off (PTO/Holiday), increasing with tenure.
403b and after 1 year of service BACS matching contribution.

About Bacs

Bay Area Community Services is a CARF accredited non-profit, community-based agency celebrating 70 years of serving Alameda, Contra Costa, Sacramento and Solano Counties by providing mental health and social services. BACS’ mission is to uplift under-served individuals and their families by doing whatever it takes. We are proud to be one of the leading agencies producing real outcomes to tough social problems. BACS owes its reputation as an innovator to our innovative and entrepreneurial staff. We are seeking individuals who want to transform clinical practice to be client-centered and effective in the field and who want to lead empowered teams to meet goals.

Founded in 2004, Brilliant Corners provides innovative housing and housing-related services to those transitioning from or at risk of homelessness or institutionalization. Our work spans major regions across California, with teams operating in Los Angeles, San Diego, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Sacramento Counties. A central responsibility will be bringing together the operational and program development functions of Housing Services ensuring alignment across regional program operations, program design and policy, quality assurance, evaluation, and client participation to build consistency statewide while preserving regional flexibility.

new_jobs.description:
The Chief Program Officer (CPO) is a senior executive and key member of BACS's Executive Team, serving as the CEO's primary service operating partner. The CPO holds full P&L responsibility and signing authority across all program operations — a $150M+ organization spanning 700+ staff, 100+ funding streams, and 100+ program, residential, and housing sites currently spanning Sacramento to San Mateo Counties. This includes the administrative and service/clinical direction of direct-service programs serving individuals with serious mental illness, substance use disorders, chronic health conditions, and housing instability or homelessness, across the full scope of care at BACS. The CPO is the operational head and primary interfacing executive with funders, county and state partners, and community stakeholders agency-wide, and ensures excellence across clinical, administrative, fiscal, compliance, human resources, and quality improvement functions. This role requires a dynamic, hands-on leader who moves fluidly between C-suite strategy and on-the-ground presence at program sites, operating with a high degree of independence and executive judgment, and who can be trusted to run agency operations at the highest standard without close oversight.

Duties And Responsibilities

Serves as the CEO's primary executive partner in leading agency-wide program operations, stepping in as a trusted #2 across strategic and operational decision-making alongside other C-suite leaders
Owns full P&L accountability for the entire program operations portfolio, including revenue, expenses, and margin performance across all funding streams; proactively identifies and acts on financial risk or underperformance
Directs that services are delivered in full compliance with all applicable funding streams (100+) and regulatory requirements across county, state, and federal contracts
Provides executive oversight, coaching, and accountability for VPs, Directors, and site leadership across the full geographic service area; monitors their performance and financial results, and reviews these with the CEO on a regular basis
Partners with Finance and HR to ensure programs are fiscally sound, appropriately staffed, and operationally compliant — with fluency in budget, HR, and compliance data sufficient to identify and resolve issues independently
Designs and enforces a consistent, high-quality service delivery model across all sites, grounded in BACS's mission, vision, and values, and centered on consumer-driven, strength-based, culturally relevant care
Leads agency-wide Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) systems and standards
Owns contract compliance, grant management, funder reporting, and funder relationships across all funding streams; reviews, negotiates, and preps major contracts for approval
Proactively identifies risk before it materializes; owns the agency-wide Risk Management Plan and associated metrics
Builds and maintains strong, trust-based relationships with funders, government partners, and community organizations
Maintains regular, visible presence across all program, residential, and housing sites agency-wide (Sacramento to San Mateo County); travels routinely as a core function of the role, and proactively communicates across internal departments without relying on others to do so
Identifies operational risk and inefficiency proactively, and acts decisively — without requiring day-to-day direction
Participates in new program development, including grant writing, funder presentations, and external representation of BACS
Leads and models a culture of accountability, excellence, and continual learning across the organization
Other duties as assigned

COMPETENCIES

Operates independently at a true C-suite level; does not require day-to-day management or micromanagement
Strong influencing and negotiating skills; excellent oral and written communication; demonstrated history of building and leveraging high-level relationships with funders, government partners, boards, and staff at all levels; politically savvy
Demonstrated P&L management experience at a large-scale, multi-program, multi-site level
Demonstrated financial, HR, compliance, and QI acumen sufficient to direct and improve agency-wide systems
High integrity and accountability; holds self and others to a standard of excellence
Resilient, adaptable, and effective in a fast-paced, high-complexity environment
Strategic thinker and visionary, balanced with a hands-on, roll-up-your-sleeves operating style
Strength-based, person-centered orientation across housing and behavioral health operations; embraces diversity in all aspects of leadership

Qualifications

Master's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related field required, along with at least ten years of progressive senior leadership experience in behavioral health, homelessness, and/or housing services, including experience operating at a COO/CPO or equivalent executive level
Demonstrated success leading large-scale, multi-site, multi-funder nonprofit or governmental operations (ideally $100M+ budget), with full P&L ownership
Demonstrated direct experience working with the full range of subpopulations served by BACS, including individuals with serious mental illness (SMI), substance use disorders (SUD), chronic and co-occurring health conditions, and housing-insecure/unhoused individuals
Strong working knowledge of behavioral health, housing, and homelessness funding and regulatory frameworks (e.g., MHSA, HUD, Medi-Cal, county contracts)
Demonstrated capacity leading diverse, multi-disciplinary teams across dispersed geographic sites
LCSW, MFT, or equivalent clinical licensure strongly preferred. Lived experience preferred
Proficiency in Microsoft Word/Excel and standard business systems

Physical Requirements

This position requires regular travel throughout the service area and frequent presence at program, residential, and housing sites, in addition to site-based work. Requires the ability to sit, stand, walk, and drive for extended periods; occasional lifting of up to 20 lbs.; dexterity for computer use and documentation; and the ability to see, hear, and speak effectively across in-person and virtual settings. This position is not remote.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Competitive salary of $300,00 -350,000 per year, exempt
100% employer-paid medical, dental, and life insurance coverage options for employees, plus a vision reimbursement program. Children’s healthcare coverage is available for as little as $25/month. Average employer-paid benefit value: approximately $913/month per enrolled individual. BACS contributions apply to company-sponsored plans only.
31 days off (PTO/Holiday), increasing with tenure.
403b and after 1 year of service BACS matching contribution.

About Bacs

Bay Area Community Services is a CARF accredited non-profit, community-based agency celebrating 70 years of serving Alameda, Contra Costa, Sacramento and Solano Counties by providing mental health and social services. BACS’ mission is to uplift under-served individuals and their families by doing whatever it takes. We are proud to be one of the leading agencies producing real outcomes to tough social problems. BACS owes its reputation as an innovator to our innovative and entrepreneurial staff. We are seeking individuals who want to transform clinical practice to be client-centered and effective in the field and who want to lead empowered teams to meet goals.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Marketing and Communications, George Mason University Costello College of Business, the Assistant Director of Marketing and Communications helps to oversee the management of marketing and communications strategies aligned with the Costello and George Mason University brands to help promote awareness of the college and its unique value proposition while driving increased levels of engagement among targeted audiences. The concepting and development of issue themes, story budgets, production and publication schedules, and vendor-provided printing, production, and mailing activities while coordinating with content developers, editors, photographers, videographers, graphic designers, and other relevant stakeholders;

On a periodic and regular basis, track, analyze data and content, and report on key metrics to evaluate and report on the effectiveness of campaigns, measure ROI, and make data-driven adjustments for optimizing performance;

Intermediate marketing skills and experience;

Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, problem-solving, organizational, and time management skills;
Advanced writing and editing skills, attention to detail and editorial style;
Possesses strong conceptual skills, a broad thinker who is able to offer a vision for moving forward;
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (e.g., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, etc.);
Ability to create and present robust, strategic, and intentional marketing and communications strategies and tactics based on organizational goals and branding guidelines;
Ability to work and make decisions in a leadership capacity, independently and as part of a team, to provide developmental guidance that ensures alignment with organizational goals and brand guidelines, among a diverse group of stakeholders that includes prospective students and their parents, current students, faculty and staff, alumni, donors, sponsors, corporate and community partners, the business community, members of the media, earned and paid media agency personnel, and representatives from other academic and administrative units across George Mason University;

Strong ability to analyze data and content, interpret results and provide relevant insights, develop actionable recommendations for optimizing for engagement and ROI, and to summarize in an executive-level reporting format;
Creativity, organization, deadline-driven enthusiasm, and an ability to articulate the vision, mission, and values of the Costello College of Business through content created for various digital and traditional platforms; and
Ability to work virtually (2 days) and on-site (3 days), and other days as the needs of the business college require.

Marketing, advertising experience;
Professional work experience in higher education strongly preferred;
Proficiency in multimedia editing software (e.g., Canva and Adobe Creative Suite software including InDesign, Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere), photography, and videography; and
Fine art, drawing, or other specialized skills.
